cor.text: Cost of revenue consists of direct costs to provide services to our customers, primarily labor costs for employees and contractors directly involved in delivering our Tokenization and Asset Servicing offerings, such as blockchain and protocol engineers and fund administrators, as well as software, systems and market data costs, validator fees, sub-advisory fees and other costs incurred as a direct result of customer transactions. Cost of revenue excludes depreciation and amortization, which is included in selling, general & administrative expenses, and any allocation of rent or utilities.

ga.heading: Selling, general & administrative
ga.text: Selling, general & administrative expenses consist of operating costs not included in the other operating cost and expense captions, primarily professional fees, share-based compensation related to warrants issued for promotional services, software, marketing, depreciation and amortization, insurance, facilities and travel, as well as acquisition-related transaction costs, including Business Combination costs required to be expensed rather than charged against additional paid-in capital.

prov.heading: Provision for expected credit losses
prov.text: Provision for expected credit losses consists of credit loss expense on our trade receivables, including amounts recognized to adjust our allowance for expected credit losses to management’s current estimate of expected credit losses and receivables written off.

nonop.heading: Interest expense
nonop.text: Interest expense was nil for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $2.0 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025. The decrease was primarily attributable to the closing of the Business Combination, upon which our outstanding convertible notes were automatically converted into shares of Old Securitize common stock, which were then immediately exchanged into shares of Company common stock, effective July 1, 2026. As a result, no interest expense was incurred on the convertible notes during the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to a full quarter of interest and accretion of debt discount in the same period in the prior year.

tax.heading: Provision for income taxes
tax.text: Provision for income taxes includes income taxes related to foreign jurisdictions and U.S. federal and state income taxes. As we conduct business activities internationally, any changes in the U.S. and foreign taxation of such activities may affect our overall provision for income taxes in the future.

net.text: Other income (expense) consists of income and expenses not directly related to our core operations, including interest expense; interest income; dividend income; loss on digital assets held for investment, net; net losses from investments held by our consolidated VIE; other income (expense), net, which consists primarily of realized and unrealized gains and losses on the Company’s other investments and foreign currency gains and losses; changes in the fair value of the option liability, SAFEs, derivative liability and earnout liabilities; and loss on settlement of convertible instruments, net.

ocf.heading: Operating Activities
ocf.text:
Net cash used in operating activities was $31.0 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to net cash used in operating activities of $11.1 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025, representing an increase in cash used of $19.9 million. Our largest source of cash provided by operating activities are revenues generated from Tokenization and Asset Servicing. Our primary uses of cash in operating activities include payments to employees for compensation, professional services, and other operating costs such as software subscriptions, insurance, and marketing, among others.

Although the net loss increased by $88.7 million, the increase was largely offset by a $75.4 million increase in non-cash adjustments to reconcile net loss to net cash used in operating activities.

sbc.heading: Share-based compensation
sbc.text:
Prior to the Business Combination, in the absence of a public trading market, our management and board of directors considered various objective and subjective factors to determine the fair value of Old Securitize’s common stock as of each grant date, including the value determined by a third party valuation firm. Following the Business Combination, the fair value of our common stock is based on its closing price on the New York Stock Exchange, and we no longer rely on third-party valuations to determine the fair value of our common stock for purposes of measuring share-based awards. We continue to use the Black-Scholes option pricing model to estimate the grant-date fair value of option grants, using the assumptions described in the Form 8-K/A.

In addition, compensation cost related to the Securitize Earnout Shares allocable to holders of assumed equity awards and warrants is measured using a Monte Carlo simulation, which requires management to make assumptions including the expected volatility of our common stock, the risk-free interest rate, the remaining term of the earnout period and the derived or requisite service period over which the related compensation cost is recognized, as appropriate. Changes in these assumptions could materially affect the fair value of these awards and the amount and timing of the related stock-based compensation expense.

wc.text: Changes in working capital resulted in $1.4 million of additional operating cash outflows compared to the prior-year period. The change primarily reflected a $10.7 million increase in cash used for prepaid expenses and other current assets, including payments under the Company’s strategic partnership agreement (refer to Note 17), a $3.5 million decrease in the amount of deferred revenue recorded as the related revenue is being recognized and a $3.3 million increase in digital assets receivable and digital assets received as consideration from operations, which represent amounts not settled in cash, partially offset by a $12.5 million decrease in contract assets as our right to the underlying payments become unconditional with the passage of time and a $8.0 million increase in accrued expenses and other current liabilities recorded. Changes in customer escrow funds and the related customer escrow funds payable substantially offset each other in both periods.

net sales.heading: Revenue
net sales.text: We generate revenue from two offerings, Tokenization and Asset Servicing. Tokenization revenue consists primarily of fees for blockchain integration services related to ecosystem expansion, together with ongoing maintenance and support, placement and distribution, fund management and trading fees. Asset Servicing revenue consists of fees for ongoing operational and administrative services provided to issuers, asset managers and investors, including recordkeeping and transfer processing, fund accounting, compliance support and investor onboarding. Refer to Note 18, Revenue, of the unaudited condensed consolidated financial statements for further details.

Tokenization.text: At Securitize, we have always had a “regulation-first” philosophy, which has led to significant investments in compliance infrastructure for the tokenization of real-world assets (“RWAs”). We expect to continue allocating significant resources to keep our practices aligned with evolving regulations in the U.S. and in the European Union, where our investment firm license from the Spanish regulator has been passported to 15 other EU countries and we have applied for a license under the EU’s DLT Pilot Regime. Other major jurisdictions, including Hong Kong, Japan, Singapore and the United Arab Emirates, are also developing frameworks that govern tokenized assets.

Asset Servicing.text: We generate revenue from two offerings, Tokenization and Asset Servicing. Tokenization revenue consists primarily of fees for blockchain integration services related to ecosystem expansion, together with ongoing maintenance and support, placement and distribution, fund management and trading fees. Refer to Note 18, Revenue, of the unaudited condensed consolidated financial statements for further details.

profile.category: Non-accelerated filer · Smaller reporting company · Emerging growth company

intro.text: Securitize Corp. (and its predecessor operations, Securitize I, Inc., formerly known as Securitize, Inc. (“Old Securitize”), collectively referred to as “Securitize”, the “Company” and “our”) operates a comprehensive platform for issuing, managing, and trading tokenized securities, including private market securities, tokenized funds and publicly traded equities using blockchain technology. The Company provides a compliance-driven infrastructure that enables the tokenization of securities, supporting functions such as dividends, distributions, share buy-backs, and investor servicing. The Company is headquartered in Miami, Florida, with operations in New York, Nevada, Spain, Israel, and Japan.

s.t: During the nine months ended September 30, 2025, certain former employees, co-founders and related parties sold shares of Old Securitize common stock and redeemable convertible preferred stock to new and existing investors at prices in excess of the estimated fair value of the shares in the 2025 secondary transactions.

At the Closing, all of Old Securitize’s outstanding convertible promissory notes, SAFEs and redeemable convertible preferred stock converted into shares of Old Securitize common stock, which were exchanged for shares of the Company’s common stock, resulting in a loss on settlement of convertible instruments, net, of $20.6 million during the three months ended September 30, 2026.

In connection with the Closing on July 1, 2026, the related preferred stock was issued and immediately converted into shares of Old Securitize common stock, which were exchanged for shares of the Company’s common stock, and we recognized a $6.7 million loss on the final remeasurement of the option liability within ‘Loss on settlement of convertible instruments, net’.

Separately, the Company holds a $ 822,258 investment in the Hamilton Lane SCOPE Securitize Tokenized Feeder, L.P., which is included in the ‘Investments’ line item on the Company's unaudited condensed consolidated balance sheets and is further described in Note 14.
